name: Caséta Smart Bridge (US)

radios.note: Lutron says it must connect to the router by Ethernet cable. Devices talk over Lutron Clear Connect RF (431-437 MHz), which is not in the radio list, so only Ethernet is recorded.

matter.note: No Matter claim found for the Smart Bridge.

apple_home.note: Lutron says only second-generation bridges (model number with a 2, such as L-BDG2) work with HomeKit. The Smart Bridge Pro 2 also works.

google_home.note: Link the Caséta Wireless service in the Google Home app.

alexa.note: Enable the Lutron Caséta skill. Lutron notes some limits, such as shades controlled by scene.

smartthings.note: No official source found in search results.

home_assistant.note: Official Lutron Caséta integration; the docs list the L-BDG2-WH and the Pro bridge. Pico remotes work as triggers; wall switch presses do not.

hubRequired.note: It is the hub. Caséta works without it for local use, but app control, schedules, Alexa, Google and Apple Home need it.

localControl.note: Lutron says local operation continues if the internet drops, but this is not recorded as a firm local-control claim.

deviceProtocols.note: Lutron Clear Connect RF at 431-437 MHz, to Caséta dimmers, switches, Pico remotes and shades.

maxDevices.note: Lutron says up to 75 wireless devices; the bridge counts as one. The Smart Bridge Pro (L-BDGPRO2) is a separate model with the same ratings.

summary: The Caséta Smart Bridge (L-BDG2) connects Lutron Caséta dimmers, switches, Pico remotes and shades to your router by Ethernet. Lutron's devices then work with Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and Home Assistant.

caveats: Lutron now calls it the Caséta Smart Hub; the L-BDG2 is the standard model and the Smart Bridge Pro is separate.
Only second-generation bridges (L-BDG2 and Pro 2) work with Apple HomeKit.
The bridge needs an Ethernet cable to the router; Lutron devices use Clear Connect RF, not Wi-Fi or Zigbee.
